newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aluminium Dunkerque holders agree restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium Dunkerque holders agree restructuring.

text.p: Pechiney has reached an agreement with other shareholders over the financial restructuring of Aluminium Dunkerque, the holding that owns the northern France-based aluminium smelter, company officials said on Friday.
"An agreement was reached on December 23," a spokesman for Aluminium Dunkerque told Reuters.
The agreement will allow Aluminium Dunkerque to return to a positive net worth position and satisfy its debt repayments obligations, he said.
At end-December 1994 Aluminium Dunkerque had a negative net worth of 184 million francs due to accumulated losses since its start up in 1992.
The losses stemmed mainly from a sharp fall in primary aluminium prices in 1993 and 1994.
Aluminium Dunkerque however expects to post a profit in 1996, the spokesman said.
French law required Aluminium Dunkerque to have a positive net worth by December 31, 1996.

The financial restructuring leaves the shareholders' structure of Aluminium Dunkerque basically unchanged, with Pechiney holding 35 percent and the balance in the hands of a group of French and international shareholders.
He said all the shareholders except Norwich, which had a 10 percent stake in the company, agreed to the plan.

This means the Norwich stake will be split among the other shareholders, which include Banque Nationale de Paris, GE Capital, AGF, Credit National, Indosuez, CIC group, CCBP, Credit Agricole, Citibank, and Legal & General.
Indosuez raised its equity stake to nine percent from 5.5.
Aluminium Dunkerque is Pechiney's newest facility with a global capacity of 215,000 tonnes per year.
The project required an initial investment of 6.2 billion francs.
